name: AlgoAlpha — high-deliverability sequence
deliverability_notes: Every step under 100 words. Brief mail looks human, not templated.
No URLs in any step. Links — especially short/tracked ones — are a top spam trigger.
No images, no attachments, no tracking pixels.
No 'Re:' on the cold initial (step 1). Spam filters watch for fake-reply subjects.
Plain text first; HTML alternative mirrors plain. No tables, no inline CSS gymnastics.
Conversational tone. Specific observation. Single question. Lowercase sign-off.
Steps 2+ use real In-Reply-To/References headers to thread under step 1.
schedule_explainer: In production each step is spaced 3-14 days apart. Stops on reply, bounce, or complaint.

steps.subject: thought on basis trades
steps.body:
hey there,

running algoalpha — small systematic shop, mostly market-neutral on crypto perps.

saw your team works on infra-adjacent stuff. quick question: who do you usually source quant research from these days? curious where the gap is.

happy to share what we've been seeing if useful.

tomás

steps.subject: thought on basis trades
steps.body:
hey,

following up briefly. no pressure.

one specific thing: BTC funding decomposed across the three biggest perp venues told a different story than spot basis last month. happy to walk through what we found if it's useful for your work.

tomás

steps.subject: thought on basis trades
steps.body:
hey,

last one for a bit.

the regime shift we tracked between mid-march and mid-april broke most classic carry models — the funding leg diverged from spot-implied basis by enough that our backtest of the standard playbook lost 60% of its PnL.

if a writeup of how we adapted would be useful, just say yes and i'll send it next week before public release.

tomás

steps.subject: one case study
steps.body:
hey,

brief case: a research operator with audience size near yours syndicated one of our notes last quarter. their engagement on the post tripled vs their baseline. eleven of their readers replied wanting direct access.

not a pitch, just sharing in case the framing is useful.

tomás

steps.subject: the 4-week window most carry models missed
steps.body:
hey,

short one. between mid-march and mid-april, BTC perp funding decoupled from the spot-implied basis by a margin most classic carry models didn't price.

the short explanation is options market makers absorbed more delta than dealers expected. the long explanation is in our latest note.

want the early read?

tomás

steps.subject: the 4-week window most carry models missed
steps.body:
hey,

quick note — the stackhouse podcast added the writeup to their reading list this week. thought you might find it relevant.

rest of the series drops over the next six weeks. want it ahead of public release?

tomás

steps.subject: your framing on basis as a liability
steps.body:
hey,

rereading your piece on basis trades. the framing of funding as a liability the long owes the short is the cleanest mental model i've seen for it — most attempts get the sign wrong on the spot leg.

if you ever want to compare risk-decomposition notes, just say so.

tomás

steps.subject: open offer
steps.body:
hey,

making this concrete.

we publish one to two long-form notes per month on systematic crypto strategies. most go behind a paywall after a week.

offer: pre-publication access for you, free, indefinitely. no NDA, no required mention.

reply yes and i'll add you.

tomás

steps.subject: summary
steps.body:
hey,

probably my last one. if the silence means not your beat, fully heard.

things i mentioned: the q1 to q2 carry break, the cross-venue spread backtest, the open offer for pre-publication research access.

wishing you a good rest of the quarter.

tomás

steps.subject: closing the loop
steps.body:
hey,

closing the loop. clearly the timing or fit isn't right and that's fine.

if our work surfaces somewhere later and you want the back-channel, you have my email.

tomás
